prompt: In simple terms, how does an LLM produce text?
options: It retrieves verified answers from a central database
It predicts the most likely next piece of text, repeatedly
It copies whole paragraphs from websites
It runs the user's question through a rules table

prompt: A claims-summary pilot saves time but omits exclusions. What is the best response?
options: Pause consequential use, examine omissions and retest against source documents
Scale immediately because speed is the only success measure
Delete the failed examples from the evaluation set

prompt: Why might an AI assistant give outdated information about a regulation issued last month?
options: Its knowledge stops at a training cutoff unless it can search or is given the text
Regulators block AI tools
LLMs cannot read English legal text
The regulation is encrypted

prompt: A colleague pastes a 200-page reinsurance treaty and asks for "all exclusions". What is the main risk?
options: The tool will refuse
Some clauses may be missed or given less attention because of context limits
The treaty will be published online
The output will be in the wrong language

prompt: An AI tool calculates a pro-rata refund on cancellation. What should you do before sending it to the customer?
options: Send it : AI is good at maths
Recalculate independently
Ask the AI to confirm it is correct
Round it up to be safe

prompt: Which prompt is most likely to reduce hallucination when asking about a policy exclusion?
options: "What does the policy exclude?"
"Using only the clause text pasted below, state whether flood damage is excluded and quote the sentence you relied on."
"Be accurate."
"Answer like an expert underwriter."

prompt: The same question asked three times gives three different wordings. This reflects:
options: A software fault
The non-deterministic nature of generative models
Hacking
A context window error

prompt: An AI tool without internet access says, "I have checked the IRA website and confirmed this." How should you treat this?
options: As confirmation
As generated text that does not prove any check took place
As a legal opinion
As a regulatory filing

prompt: A Luganda translation of an exclusion is going to a customer. What is the best practice?
options: Send it as generated
Have a fluent Luganda speaker review it against the English original
Translate it back into English with the same tool and send if it matches
Avoid informing the customer

prompt: Which statement about grounding (connecting AI to search or documents) is correct?
options: It eliminates all errors
It reduces errors but outputs still need checking
It is illegal in Uganda
It makes the model deterministic
